title: CPI(M) hails Kerala High Court relief to protesting Sanskrit University students as a slap in the face to the VC and UDF government

ai.summary: CPI(M) called Kerala High Court's order lifting suspension of 16 Sanskrit University students a 'resounding slap' for the education minister and vice-chancellor, accusing them of siding with Sangh Parivar.

facts.claim: Kerala High Court quashed suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit
facts.quote: the Kerala High Court’s order quashing the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in Kalady

facts.claim: CPI(M) accused education minister Roji M. John of aiding the vice-chancellor
facts.quote: Mr. John had actively aided the vice-chancellor, whom he portrayed as a Sangh Parivar enabler

facts.claim: CPI(M) said the students were Student Federation of India activists
facts.quote: all Student Federation of India (SFI) activists

facts.claim: CPI(M) accused minister of demanding students apologize to vice-chancellor
facts.quote: Mr. John had revealed his true political colours. He demanded the students apologise to the vice-chancellor or forfeit their future

facts.claim: CPI(M) compared minister's demand to RSS leaders apologizing to colonial rulers
facts.quote: His demand was a hark back to the tradition of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leaders to apologise to colonial rulers

facts.claim: CPI(M) said High Court ordered special exams for students
facts.quote: the High Court directive to conduct special examinations for the striking students

facts.claim: CPI(M) said students were from working-class families
CPI(M) said students were punished for demanding campus infrastructure
facts.quote: He said the students had been punished for demanding basic campus infrastructure, including the lack of lecturers and delay in awarding fellowships

ai.background_note: Kerala High Court lifted suspension of 16 Sanskrit University students who were Student Federation of India activists, after the education minister and vice-chancellor demanded they apologize for alleged misconduct.
